text: Jumping straight into SQL for three staging models, and discovering halfway through that the naming or source declarations are inconsistent, is a real and avoidable cost. This lesson plans all three first.

Every staging model starts from a declared source, never a bare table name. One sources yml file makes source calls resolve anywhere in the project, and makes the raw table show up in the lineage graph later.

The naming convention is stg, source name, double underscore, table name. That disambiguation matters once more than one source feeds staging models — which this platform adds later, in the Python ingestion chapter.

A staging model's job stays narrow on purpose: rename columns, light type casting, one source table at a time. No joins, no aggregation, no business logic — that's the intermediate and mart layer's job in Lesson 9.
This narrow scope is exactly what lets a later schema change ripple through cleanly instead of unpredictably. Next: turning this plan into the three real staging models.
